# The Moon That Turns Its Face

## Scripture

*"When I consider your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars, which you have set in place, what is mankind that you are mindful of them, human beings that you care for them?" — Psalm 8:3–4 (NIV)*

## Reflection

Step outside on a clear November night and find the moon. Perhaps it's a thin crescent, perhaps nearly full. Either way, you're only ever seeing one face. The moon rotates in perfect sync with its orbit, so the same side always turns toward Earth. The far side—the one we never see—remains hidden, though it is just as real, just as cratered and rugged as the side we know.

There is something deeply comforting in that quiet faithfulness. The moon doesn't turn away. Night after night, season after season, it presents itself steadily to us, reflecting the sun's light into our darkness.

The psalmist looked up and felt small—and yet marveled that God was mindful of him. We might feel the same: so much of our own lives feels like the far side of the moon, hidden even from ourselves, known fully only to God. But here is the promise: the One who set the moon in its faithful dance knows every hidden side of us. Nothing in us is unseen to Him. And like that borrowed moonlight, whatever light we carry is not our own—it is His, reflected.

## Prayer

Lord, when I feel hidden or forgotten, remind me that You see the far side of my heart and still hold me close. Thank You for the moon's quiet faithfulness—a picture of Your steady care. Help me reflect Your light into the darkness around me tonight. Amen.
